title: Gate a tokenizer and model release
description: Choose a candidate and release policy, then change its traffic share. Exact contract failures must remain visible even when average cost or quality looks acceptable.

policies.label: Contract-first gate
policies.detail: Requires exact IDs, offsets, special-token mapping, template identity, protected-slice quality, and a ready rollback.

policies.label: Averages-only gate
policies.detail: A deliberately weak policy that checks aggregate cost and task score but ignores exact compatibility.

candidates.label: Identical bundle repack
candidates.detail: Container and library packaging changed; approved tokenizer artifacts and model contract did not.
candidates.failureTruth: No contract drift is present in the fixtures. Production canary evidence still checks runtime behavior.

candidates.label: Chat template changed
candidates.detail: Vocabulary IDs match, but role separators and serialized control-token order changed.
candidates.failureTruth: Aggregate quality nearly passes, yet production prompts no longer match the role structure the checkpoint was approved with.

candidates.label: Normalizer reduces token count
candidates.detail: Compatibility normalization shortens some inputs while changing code points and source alignment.
candidates.failureTruth: The attractive token saving hides changed text identity, broken offsets, and protected-slice quality loss.

candidates.label: Vocabulary IDs remapped
candidates.detail: Existing token strings received different integer IDs without retraining the model's embedding rows.
candidates.failureTruth: The model reads unrelated embedding rows. This is a correctness incident, not a canary optimization.
